# NocoBase 3 repository migration

NocoBase 3 is maintained in `nocobase/nocobase` on `v3-develop`, with stable promotion to `v3-main`. The repository's default branch is `main`, which continues to maintain the v1/v2 line. See `skills/README.md` for global Skill installation commands using the lightweight `nocobase/skills-v3` distribution.

Regular v3 development branches use `<type>/v3-<name>`, such as `feat/v3-app-installer` or `fix/v3-release-routing`. Quality, changeset, Docs and UI Library checks accept pull requests targeting these branches, with their existing path filters, so stacked pull requests receive the same checks as pull requests targeting `v3-develop` or `v3-main`; pushes continue to run these checks only on `v3-develop`, and the stable guard continues to run only for pull requests targeting `v3-main`. GitHub Actions expresses the stacked target as the glob `*/v3-*`; for a valid branch under this rule, with a non-empty type and name and no extra slash, that is equivalent to the bot and CI regular expression `/^[^/]+\/v3-[^/]+$/`.

## Release routing

Executable v3 workflows live directly in `.github/workflows/` and use the `v3-` filename prefix. Their corresponding entries on `main` dispatch the implementation on `v3-develop`. An implementation-only change needs a check that this dispatch still reaches it; input, trigger, or filename changes need a coordinated update of the entry on `main` too.

PR checks are selected from the pull request's workflow context, not from the default branch's workflow inventory. Changeset has no dispatcher on `main`, and Quality has no workflow in this repository at all: `nocobase-bot` forwards pull requests to v3 targets from branches of this repository, and pushes to `v3-develop` whose head commit does not contain `[skip ci]`, to `nocobase3-quality.yml` in `chenos/nocobase-ci`, and mirrors its jobs as the checks `Changed files`, `Typecheck`, `Test`, `Build`, `Create-app smoke (default)`, `Create-app smoke (examples)`, `App-installer smoke` and `quality`. That workflow is the only definition of these checks, so a change to them is made there; a check that needs a new script in this repository should tolerate the script's absence, or land after the change that adds it. Fork pull requests get no Quality check. The `PR description` check (`v3-pr-description.yml`) is an ordinary pull request workflow of this repository rather than a forwarded one: it needs no dependencies or secrets, and only GitHub's own `edited` event can rerun it when a description changes; like Changeset, it has no entry on `main`. The Docs and UI Library entries on `main` accept only manual dispatch and forward it to `v3-develop`; changes to their source-side PR branch filters do not change that entry contract. Keep their filenames, dispatch inputs and destination synchronized when those change.

| Workflow                                                                               | Source and destination                                                                                                                                   | Registry or output                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v3-release-beta.yml`                                                                  | Release `v3-develop` after Pro `develop` passed with the candidate, then merge version commits back there; then release Pro beta (`skip_pro` skips both) | Public npm, `beta` and `latest` dist-tags; Pro registry                                                                 |
| `v3-merge-beta-to-stable.yml`                                                          | Promote `v3-develop` into `v3-main`, then synchronize prerelease state back                                                                              | Version promotion only                                                                                                  |
| `v3-release-stable.yml`                                                                | Release `v3-main`, then synchronize back to `v3-develop`; an older branch uses `keep_latest`                                                             | Public npm, `latest` or `legacy` dist-tag                                                                               |
| `v3-github-release.yml`                                                                | Aggregate `nocobase-v3-beta/*`, legacy `release-beta/*` or `release/*` tags                                                                              | GitHub Release without taking the shared Latest marker, and the release's changelog entry on nocobase/website-v3 `main` |
| `v3-pro-release-beta.yml`, `v3-pro-release-stable.yml`, `v3-pro-promote-to-stable.yml` | The independent `nocobase/nocobase3-pro` repository, retaining its `develop` and `main` branches; OSS pins come from `v3-develop` and `v3-main`          | The configured private Pro registry                                                                                     |

`v3-release-beta.yml` releases Pro beta in the same run: its `pro-candidate` job tests Pro `develop` against the release candidate, and the open-source packages are published only after it passes. When Pro has something to release (pending changesets, or published `@nocobase/*` ranges that reject the release), it names the Pro release, writes its section of Pro's root `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md` and `CHANGELOG.ja-JP.md` with `scripts/changelog.mjs` exactly as `v3-pro-release-beta.yml` does, builds and tests that tree, and pushes it to `release-candidate/<batch>` in `nocobase/nocobase3-pro`, with the release tag and the URL of the run (`OSS-Run`) in the commit message. After npm, `pro-release` checks the versions against pkg-v3 with `check-release-versions.mjs --candidate` and reserves their `name@version` tags at the candidate, and only then tags it `release-beta/<batch>`, publishes exactly that commit, deletes the untagged candidates of earlier batches it superseded, merges current Pro `develop` into its release branch (taking `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` from develop, then re-syncing the upstream blocks and regenerating the lockfile against the new pointer: the merged release commit on `v3-develop`, or develop's own pointer when develop was already bumped to a descendant of it, so the merge back never moves develop's pointer backwards; a develop pointer that is neither is replaced by the merged release commit with a warning) and the release branch into Pro `develop`, and deletes the candidate branch. A `name@version` tag left at a commit no release tag points at, for a version pkg-v3 does not have, belongs to an attempt that never published and is moved to the new candidate with a warning; a published version tagged elsewhere fails. Each step that writes to the Pro repository puts the write token in the remote itself and removes it when it ends, and no install runs with it. `scripts/pro-release-candidates.mjs` decides which candidates are still in flight: one is done once a `release-beta/*` tag points at its commit and Pro `develop` contains it, and stale once it is older than 30 days (GitHub can no longer re-run its run). `pro-candidate` prunes done and stale candidates of earlier batches just before it pushes a new one, `pro-release` also prunes the untagged ones once its Pro beta is published (their runs can no longer publish), and the standalone `v3-pro-release-beta.yml` and `v3-pro-promote-to-stable.yml` refuse to start while any candidate is in flight, ignoring stale ones and linking each blocking one to the run that pushed it; as a second line of defence, `pro-release` refuses to publish when a Pro release tag appeared after Pro `develop` was tested. Nothing deletes a candidate on failure or cancellation, so "Re-run failed jobs" is the supported recovery from any failure: it reuses the earlier jobs' outputs and the same open-source release candidate, and every step it repeats continues from the tags, branches, published versions, and merges an earlier attempt already made. `build`, `test`, `smoke`, `pro-candidate`, and `release` download artifacts kept for 7 days, so they can be re-run only within 7 days; `pro-release` and `github-release` read only job outputs and can be re-run for as long as GitHub allows, 30 days. The Pro jobs keep commercial source out of artifacts and caches; it reaches only the private Pro repository (`tests/scripts/pro-release-workflow-policy.test.mjs`). The dedicated Pro workflows remain for Pro-only, stable and promotion runs; the Pro repository has no release workflows of its own.

`release-beta/*` and `release/*` remain internal release candidate branch names. New OSS Beta aggregate tags use `nocobase-v3-beta/*`, with GitHub Release titles `NocoBase v3 Beta · <batch>`; stable tags remain `release/*`. Batch numbering and changelog selection accept both Beta tag prefixes. Renamed historical tags read the original changelog headings from their immutable commits. They are not replacements for the long-lived v3 branches. The Pro submodule path `vendor/nocobase3` remains a directory name, not an OSS repository address.

## V2 workflow entries on v3-develop

`main` is currently the default branch, and `v3-develop` is planned to replace it. GitHub only lets a `workflow_dispatch` workflow be run manually when a file of that name exists on the default branch, so `v3-develop` already carries a thin entry for each v1/v2 manual workflow still in use: `auto-merge.yml`, `build-pro-image.yml`, `changelog-and-release.yml`, `manual-build-pro-image.yml`, `manual-build-pro-plugin-image.yml`, `manual-merge.yml`, `manual-npm-publish-license-kit.yml`, `manual-npm-publish.yml`, `manual-release-develop.yml`, `manual-release-next.yml`, `manual-release-v1.yml`, `manual-release.yml`, `nocobase-test-backend.yml`, `rebuild-docker-nodefix.yml`, `release.yml` and `test-feishu-notify.yml`. They keep their v1/v2 filenames, without the `v3-` prefix that v3 workflows use, and each one dispatches the same file on `main` with the same inputs; the implementation stays on `main` and is not copied. To run one on `next`, `develop`, `v1` or a feature branch, choose that branch in "Use workflow from". These entries do nothing before the switch, because the default branch's own file is the one that runs.

When a v1/v2 workflow on `main` adds, removes or renames a `workflow_dispatch` workflow, or changes its name or inputs, update the entry on `v3-develop` first and then `main`. The five manual workflows that have never run (`build-docker.yml`, `build-internal-image.yml`, `create-branch.yml`, `manual-build-pr-docker-image.yml` and `manual-e2e.yml`) have no entry on purpose; the list is `EXCLUDED` in `scripts/check-v2-workflow-entries.mjs`.

Drift is checked automatically by `scripts/check-v2-workflow-entries.mjs`. The `V3 V2 Workflow Entries` workflow on `v3-develop` runs it on pull requests that touch workflows (a mismatch with `main` is a warning there, since an entry may land before `main` follows), daily once `v3-develop` is the default branch, and on demand (a mismatch is an error). The `V2 workflow entries` workflow on `main` runs it on every pull request that touches `.github/workflows/` and fails on a mismatch, so a `main` change to a manual workflow cannot merge before its entry exists on `v3-develop`.

## Repository configuration to confirm

The source workflows already target the new OSS repository and public npm. Repository-level settings are separate from committed YAML; a maintainer must confirm the following on `nocobase/nocobase` before treating a release as operational. Local checks do not prove that secrets exist or that publishing permissions have been granted.

- The NocoBase GitHub App is installed for `nocobase/nocobase`; `NOCOBASE_APP_ID` and `NOCOBASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are configured, with the contents and pull request permissions the release workflows require. Pro workflows also require App access to the independent Pro repository.
- `NPM_TOKEN` can publish the affected public `@nocobase` packages. Pro uses `PRO_NPM_REGISTRY` and `PRO_NPM_TOKEN` independently and must keep using its private registry.
- Branch protection and required checks refer to the `v3-` workflows and allow the configured release bot's squash merges and synchronization into `v3-develop` and `v3-main`.
- Default-branch dispatch entries are present on `main`, Actions is enabled, and the beta and stable workflows pass with `dry_run: true` before an actual publish. Pro dispatch input descriptions on `main` should name the OSS `v3-develop` / `v3-main` branches; their current descriptions still use the former OSS names, although dispatch already selects `v3-develop`.
- `RELEASE_RESULT_FEISHU_WEBHOOK_URL` is configured if internal release notifications are required.
- Documentation deployment uses the independent repository secrets `V3_DOCS_ALI_OSS_BUCKET`, `V3_DOCS_ALI_OSS_REGION` and `V3_DOCS_ALI_CDN_DOMAIN`; leave the existing v2 deployment targets unchanged. Documentation and UI Library share `DOCS_ALI_OSS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `DOCS_ALI_OSS_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET`, which must have access to their respective destinations. UI Library keeps its `nocobase-ui-library` bucket in `cn-beijing`. Both workflows publish on matching pushes to `v3-develop`, or when manually dispatched with `publish` enabled; no additional migration variable is required.
- Pull requests changing only `docs/**` skip Quality, Changeset Check and Guard Main; the Docs workflow checks and builds the documentation without publishing. Quality also skips documentation-only pushes to `v3-develop`, where Docs builds and publishes instead; the forwarded Quality reports its checks as skipped rather than leaving them out. Mixed changes retain the normal checks. These workflow-level path filters must be considered before making the skipped workflows required branch checks, because GitHub can leave required checks pending when a workflow is filtered out. Preview routing is managed separately by the bot.

## Historical references

Published `CHANGELOG.md` entries and consumed `.changeset/pre/` files retain links to the archived OSS repository as release history. Pro release-note conversion also accepts archived OSS links so those historical notes still point to their Pro source. These references and the independent Pro repository are intentional; current package metadata, installation commands, and usage links must point to `nocobase/nocobase` and select a v3 branch where needed.

## Skills distribution synchronization

`v3-skills-sync.yml` on `v3-develop` reacts to `skills/**` pushes and manual dispatch. It uses the existing NocoBase GitHub App to send `skills-updated` to `nocobase/skills-v3`, scoped to contents-write on that repository alone. The target's workflow reads the latest source skills subtree and commits changed content using its own token; it performs no scheduled polling. Confirm the App installation covers `skills-v3`, Actions permits contents writes there, and notification and target runs both succeed.

The paired `main` entry has the same filename, exposes `workflow_dispatch` with no inputs and forwards to `v3-develop`. Merge the implementation before the default-branch entry; until both land, invoke the target's manual workflow for recovery. A source notification success means only that dispatch was accepted, so inspect the target run before treating synchronization as complete. Root Skills remain released by merge and must not describe npm features that have not shipped.
